newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian state selling cement firm stake.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian state selling cement firm stake.

text.p: National Bank of Egypt (NBE) said on Monday it and other public-sector companies would sell about 8.2 million shares in Suez Cement, 17 percent of the company, in the form of global depository receipts (GDRs) through the London stock exchange, probably in December.
Salomon Brothers will be the lead manager and international coordinator for the transaction, which will be worth about $125 million at the current price on the Egyptian stock exchange.

It will be the second ever GDR issue for an Egyptian company. In July ING Barings managed the sale of shares worth about $120 million in Commercial International Bank (CIB), also for National Bank of Egypt.

NBE chairman Mahmoud Abdel Aziz told a news conference NBE would sell 4.2 million of its shares in Suez Cement, Egypt's other three public-sector retail banks would sell one million each and Assiut Cement, a subsidiary of the state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries, a further one million.
The other retail banks are Bank of Alexandria, Banque Misr and Banque du Caire.
The GDR issue will cut the Egyptian state's shareholding in Suez Cement to less than 60 percent.

The state has already floated about 23 percent of the company on the Egyptian stock exchange and some of the shares are owned by partially privatised cement companies like Egyptian Tora Portland Cement (7.35 percent), Alexandria Portland Cement (7.35 percent) and Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA (7.20 percent).
Suez Cement has been one of the most profitable of Egyptian cement companies, itself a highly profitable sector.

NBE said that in the first six months of 1996 it made a net profit of 151 million pounds on sales of 237 million, compared with a net profit of 280 million and sales of 466 million in the whole of calendar 1995.

The company now has total production capacity of 2.9 million tonnes a year from its two plants. It is expanding the capacity of its Suez plant to 1.2 million tonnes a year from one million and is building a third plant with a capacity of 1.35 million.
NBE said that the international GDR sale might be coupled with another local share offering in Suez Cement.
It said that other international banks would be chosen to help with the issue within a week and that a bank had yet to be chosen to act as depository.
"In principle it has been agreed that the GDR offer will take place in December, on a timetable to be announced within the next few weeks," the bank added.
